statement.title: Evidence and innovative strategies for policies that foster inclusive growth and educational reform.
paragraphs: In many ways and at most institutional sites, education is still relatively untouched by technology. Changes sometimes seem insignificant and the results disappointing. We make the case for the transformative power of technology in learning — and test it, cost it and appraise it before money is committed.
Our education work runs from primary schools to madrasahs, technical and vocational training and the management of the programs that fund them.

scene.title: Five stages of a learning system, each one appraised.
scene.lead: Each step names an assignment on the record. Together they cover the ladder from the first classroom to the skills a changing economy needs.

steps.label: Primary
steps.title: Appraising digital learning for primary schools
steps.text: Feasibility for NextGen primary education in Bangladesh for the Asian Development Bank, including the technical feasibility and cost-benefit models for digital and AI-powered learning and assessment.

steps.label: Secondary
steps.title: Appraising secondary and madrasah education
steps.text: Economic and financial feasibility for new secondary and madrasah education projects, with market analysis, cost-benefit assessment, risk modeling and an evaluation of institutional capacity, aligned with national development priorities and ADB guidelines.
points: ENPV and FNPV, EIRR and FIRR and benefit-cost ratios
Excel models and narratives for Planning Commission-format feasibility reports

steps.label: Madrasah
steps.title: Costing a modern madrasah education
steps.text: Technical, financial and institutional feasibility for secondary and higher-secondary madrasah education, including costed plans for ICT labs, science labs and solar learning environments.

steps.label: Skills
steps.title: Building the investment case for skills
steps.text: Economic and financial appraisal, costing and financing analysis for technical and vocational education and training, including sections of a Planning Commission-compliant feasibility report.

steps.label: Systems
steps.title: Management that can deliver the program
steps.text: An assessment of management capacity in ADB’s education and skills programs (SESIP, SEIP): consultation synthesis and an assessment of institutional capacity and government systems.
points: Training government officials and institutional leaders in policy formulation and implementation
Tools and methodologies for continuous learning and improvement

practice.eyebrow: How we work on learning systems
practice.title: From a pilot to a program that lasts.

rows.title: Program design and scaling
points: Program frameworks aligned with policy and development goals
Theory of Change and logical frameworks to guide design
Sustainability, scalability and impact measurement built into program planning
Support for pilot programs and their transition to full-scale implementation

rows.title: Economic and financial feasibility
points: Economic and financial modeling to evaluate project viability and potential returns
Cost-benefit analysis and financial forecasting for public and private investment
Strategic financial planning, including long-term investment roadmaps and funding strategies

rows.title: Evaluation built for education
rows.text: Targeted evaluation approaches for key sectors, education among them, aligned with regional priorities and national policies — combining econometric and statistical analysis with qualitative methods such as Most Significant Change and participatory research.

rows.title: Digital proficiency
rows.text: Training programs for public officials, policymakers and private-sector stakeholders on using digital tools effectively.
